parts.label: (a)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Find $t = 0.25\text{ ms}$ on the time axis of Fig. 6.2, go straight up to the curve and then straight across to read the signal voltage in $\text{mV}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the sampled voltage**
Think of the ADC as taking a snapshot. At $t = 0.25\text{ ms}$ the curve in Fig. 6.2 passes through $5.0\text{ mV}$.

Step 2: **Convert to 4-bit binary**
With the smallest bit representing $1.0\text{ mV}$, the number is just the voltage value in binary. $$5 = 4 + 1 = 0101$$ So the ADC outputs $0101$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Find $t = 1.25\text{ ms}$ on Fig. 6.2 and read across to the voltage axis, remembering the ADC can only output whole $1.0\text{ mV}$ steps so you take the whole-number level.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the sampled voltage**
At $t = 1.25\text{ ms}$ the smooth curve is at about $8$ to $9\text{ mV}$. The ADC only records complete $1.0\text{ mV}$ levels, so this sample is recorded as $8\text{ mV}$.

Step 2: **Convert to 4-bit binary**
Write 8 as a 4-bit binary number: $$8 = 8 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1000$$ So the ADC outputs $1000$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: List the sampling times from $t = 0$ to $t = 1.50\text{ ms}$ using the given $0.25\text{ ms}$ interval and read each corresponding voltage from Fig. 6.2.
Hint 2: Round each reading down to the nearest whole $1.0\text{ mV}$ level, since that is what the 4-bit ADC can store.
Hint 3: Remember what a DAC does between samples - it holds its last value constant until the next sample arrives, so think about the shape this makes.
Hint 4: Check the vertical scale on Fig. 6.3 is in $\text{mV}$ and the horizontal steps must line up exactly with $0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50\text{ ms}$.
parts.proper_answer: Staircase with horizontal steps changing at every $0.25\text{ ms}$: 0 mV (0-0.25 ms), 5 mV (0.25-0.50 ms), 10 mV (0.50-0.75 ms), 12 mV (0.75-1.00 ms), 15 mV (1.00-1.25 ms), 8 mV (1.25-1.50 ms).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Sample the original at every 0.25 ms**
You are taking snapshots of Fig. 6.2. Reading across gives roughly: $$t = 0: 0\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 0.25\text{ ms}: 5\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 0.50\text{ ms}: 10\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 0.75\text{ ms}: 12\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 1.00\text{ ms}: 15\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 1.25\text{ ms}: 8\text{ mV}$$ $$t = 1.50\text{ ms}: 5\text{ mV}$$

Step 2: **Hold each value until the next sample**
A DAC cannot follow the smooth curve. It outputs the last received digital level as a steady voltage, then jumps suddenly when the next sample arrives. That is why the reconstruction is a series of flat horizontal steps, not a smooth line.

Step 3: **Draw the staircase on Fig. 6.3**
Start at 0 mV from $t = 0$ to $0.25\text{ ms}$, then jump to 5 mV to $0.50\text{ ms}$, then 10 mV to $0.75\text{ ms}$, then 12 mV to $1.00\text{ ms}$, then 15 mV to $1.25\text{ ms}$, then 8 mV to $1.50\text{ ms}$. Each vertical change lines up exactly with a multiple of $0.25\text{ ms}$ with no time delay.
